claims.statement: For a finite family of positive block sizes s_i with M=sum_i s_i and coefficient sequences f_i(t)>=binom(s_i,t), the product coefficient [z^k] product_i(sum_t f_i(t)z^t), divided by binom(M,k), equals the expectation of product_i(f_i(K_i)/binom(s_i,K_i)) under the multivariate hypergeometric count-vector law of a uniform k-subset, for 0<=k<=M. Finite Jensen and log(w)>=2(w-1)/(w+1) for w>=1 yield the registered exponent lower bound; for f_i(t)=binom(s_i,t)+1[t=1], this specializes to the singleton-occupancy exponent.
claims.scope: Finite-block coefficient identity and informal Jensen/Taylor consequence only; empty family is handled at M=k=0. No parent rank, marked-deletion identity, selector, selected MASS, payment, aggregate or arbitrary-tree conclusion.
claims.reason: The exact count-vector identity follows by finite coefficient convolution and Vandermonde normalization. The Jensen, logarithm and Taylor steps are stated with their domains and remain an informal proof route; the sealed center-subset Lean theorem proves only its exact polynomial expansion.

limitations: No formal verification of the count-vector/Jensen bridge was performed.
Coefficient domination does not transfer parent rank, marked-deletion identities, original tag multiplicities or strict current-p selectors to a larger graph class.
No conclusion is proposed for selected MASS, exact-ratio payment, the primary predicate, or the global Erdős993 target.
